title: Augmentation axis computes the characterized sheaf cup product
statement: For an arbitrary family U of opens of a scheme X, a computing resolution pairing D [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], comparison data A,B,C [def-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-data], and a bilinear cup satisfying IsModuleCupProduct [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product], the product of inverse-iso images of the beta homology classes of Cech cycles a,b equals the inverse-iso image of the beta class of any cycle c whose underlying cochain is cechCupCochain(a,b) [def-sc-cech-cup-product]. Only the augmentation axis is asserted; no existence or alpha formula for a total homology pairing is asserted.

source.place: final diagram; signed total construction of Tag 07MB

proof.text: Obtain the signed total homology pairing and its alpha and beta formulas from the chain-map component equations. This construction uses no sheaf cohomology cup or comparison isomorphism.

The projection of kernel cycles to homology is surjective (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective); alpha is a quasi-isomorphism, so its homology map is invertible. Lift the two beta classes to global resolution cycles. Leibniz shows D.pair of these cycles is a cycle. The alpha_class equations identify the inverse comparison images of the beta classes with the classes of these lifts.

Evaluate the same total pairing on these lifts with its alpha formula and on the original Cech cycles with its beta formula. Apply the inverse target iso and its alpha_class equation to identify the two target classes. The characterization hcup now gives precisely the asserted product equality.
